summary.headline: Yatra Q1 FY27 gross bookings rose 17% to INR21,007 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell 39% to INR151 million on MICE disruption and Kanoo build-out costs.
summary.overview: Gross bookings grew about 17% YoY to INR21,007 million and gross margin rose 6.1% to INR1,227 million, while revenue from operations fell 10.4% to INR1,879 million as MICE top line dropped about INR300 million. Adjusted EBITDA declined 39.4% to INR151 million (12.29% of gross margin) and PAT was INR3.4 million. Management attributed the margin squeeze to temporary MICE disruption, air margin pressure from delayed Middle East airline PLB deals, and pre-revenue people and platform costs for the Kanoo partnership. No FY27 guidance was issued; management said it expects to provide guidance next quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and cash equivalents plus term deposits

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: Gross bookings INR16,579 million (+17.6%) and gross margin INR699 million (+8%), with take rate down from 4.6% to 4.2%. Passenger volume grew 4.8% to 1.264 million, about twice industry growth.

segments.name: Hotels and Packages
segments.commentary: Gross bookings INR3,876 million (+13%) and gross margin INR386 million (+24%), margin up to 9.95%. Standalone hotels: gross bookings +34%, revenue +62%, room nights +30%.

segments.name: MICE
segments.commentary: Top line about INR300 million lower YoY due to international group travel disruption; about INR60 million gross margin hit (INR30 million from lower TTV, INR30 million from domestic competition). Management says Q2 MICE volumes are about 50% above Q1.

segments.name: Corporate and Travel Pro
segments.commentary: 53 new corporate customers with expected annual billable potential of about INR2,223 million; 30-plus logos (about INR800 million, per CEO; INR80 crore of INR140 crore per the Q&A answer) came via Travel Pro. Corporate net retention cited at 97%.

segments.name: RECAP (expense management)
segments.commentary: More than 20 customers added since launch; no financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 guidance given; management expects to issue guidance next quarter once the market stabilises.
Second half of FY27: air margins expected to recover as Middle East airline PLB deals close and capacity returns; management expects adjusted EBITDA margin close to 20% in H2 before scaling again.
Q2 FY27: MICE pipeline stronger and margins healthier; margins expected to be range-bound with marginal improvement, Kanoo contribution-positive from Q2.
Medium term: adjusted EBITDA margin back to 20%-plus, then 30% range over time.
Air-to-hotel gross margin mix about 60:40 today; 50:50 target over the next 2-3 years reiterated.
capex_capacity: Kanoo Travel partnership extends corporate platform into the Middle East; revenue began around 1 July or mid-July 2026, with people hiring, training, infrastructure and GCP cloud hosting costs incurred in Q1.
Management said people costs will stay at Q1 absolute levels in Q2 while Kanoo revenue ramps.
Technology investments in platform stability and response times said to have lifted B2C performance.
Hotel supply expansion described as a strategic priority, supporting standalone hotel growth.
Management said capacity was built ahead of expected revenue across Travel Pro, RECAP and Kanoo.
demand_pricing: Domestic travel resilient; air passenger traffic in India grew about 2.3% YoY in the period per management.
International and MICE hit by West Asia conflict; industry inquiries for some international destinations down roughly 10% to 15%.
Airfares elevated: ATPs 20% to 30% higher on some routes due to European transit and rerouting.
Share of international business fell to under 30% of mix, from late 30s to near 40% previously.
B2C share rose and travel agency volumes grew; corporate share fell slightly. B2B mix moved from late 60s to mid-60s percent.
Customer promotion as a percentage of gross bookings at about a five-quarter high, attributed to B2C mix and discounting.
Middle East as an endpoint under 20% of business; including transit, 30%-plus of international travel transits the region.

qa_highlights.question: Will air margins stay subdued for FY27 given supply cuts and incentive timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East carriers have not closed annual PLB deals, so revenue is recognised at lower rates; capacity is normalising and margins are expected to improve in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is MICE revenue loss recoverable in the next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MICE restructuring from international to domestic group travel is over; Q2 volumes are about 50% above Q1 with better margin profile.

qa_highlights.question: Can Travel Pro bookings run at about INR200 crore and are contracts multi-year?
qa_highlights.answer: Travel Pro projects are mostly annual contracts versus two to three years for Elite; Travel Pro Q2 trend 20-30% higher; corporate net retention 97%.

qa_highlights.question: How is MICE contribution to profit and what is the long-run profit mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MICE carries about 9-10% gross margin and 40-plus% operating margin; it should account for about 20-25% of profit, not 50%. Q1 MICE impact estimated at INR4-5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Hiring, training and infrastructure for Kanoo were incurred in Q1 before revenue; absolute people costs stay at these levels, with revenue contribution from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate restructuring (Yatra India merger with parent) timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said work has continued for about six quarters across India, Singapore, Cyprus, Cayman and SEC; no timeline given as regulator timing is hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: Corporate card product and working capital plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Working with banks on a product that balances MDR of about 165 bps against shorter credit cycles; also working with Amex, HDFC/Citi and SBI on card platforms, targeting airlines and hotels to bear card cost. Long lead time.

risks_watch: Air margin recovery depends on Middle East carriers closing annual PLB deals and capacity normalising; management expects H2 improvement but Q2 likely range-bound.

MICE recovery: Q2 volumes said to be about 50% above Q1, but management did not quantify a timeline to recover the roughly INR300 million YoY top-line loss; MICE is lumpy and disproportionately profitable.
Kanoo cost base: people costs stay at Q1 absolute levels in Q2 while Kanoo revenue begins; Kanoo expected to be contribution-positive from Q2, which needs verification.
No FY27 guidance; management plans to issue guidance next quarter once markets stabilise. Watch whether the H2 adjusted EBITDA margin near 20% target is delivered.
Working capital and corporate card: MDR of about 165 bps versus shorter credit cycles unresolved; long lead time with banks (Amex, HDFC/Citi, SBI). Also the US parent-India merger has no timeline.
key_quotes: So my sense at this point based on what trending we are seeing is that in the second half of the year, we should start being pretty close to the 20% mark before scaling up again from there.
We haven't given any guidance for the current year, Sonal.
So it's under 30% at the moment.
If I was to give you a sense of a timeline, having seen how regulators in different markets behave, it's very hard to give an exact timeline on that.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the medium-term story (MICE rebound, air margin recovery in H2, 20%-plus margin path) but cautious and evasive on specifics: no FY27 guidance, no timeline for the India-parent merger, and no timeline for recovering the MICE revenue loss. Its explanations for the margin decline (MICE, air PLBs, Kanoo costs) were detailed, but the forward dates remained hedged.
